title: RAW source sketch: complete Vitruvius IX.8.9 coupling and month-index passage
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. Keeps the entire owned IX.8.9 paragraph: water-driven float rise couples to counterweight descent, axis/wheel rotation, seasonal display, and a sun index through month/day holes. This is a bounded operational source sketch from RAW394, with no target or dimensional flow model. The old longer source and its HTML artifact remain unchanged.

complete_selected_source.work: Vitruvius De architectura IX.8.9, complete paragraph in the already owned Gwilt English translation
complete_selected_source.text: 9. Thus as the phellos ascends by the action of the water, the counterpoise of sand descends and turns the axis, as does that the wheel, whose rotation causes at times the greater part of the circle of the zodiac to be in motion, and at other times the smaller; thus adjusting the hours to the seasons. Moreover in the sign of each month are as many holes as there are days in it, and the index which in dials is generally a representation of the sun, shews the spaces of the hours; and whilst passing from one hole to another, it completes the period of the month.
complete_selected_source.boundary: From 9. Thus as the phellos ascends... through ...it completes the period of the month. No clause within this paragraph is dropped.
complete_selected_source.context: The §8 chain, float/phellos, equal sand counterweight, axle and marked zodiac wheel are inherited apparatus declarations; §10 transitions to water management, and §§11-15 describe the regulator. No prior analemma construction or regulator is silently claimed to be fully translated by this paragraph.
complete_selected_source.historical_limits: Ancient work, late first century BCE; owned text is the later public-domain Gwilt English translation hosted by LacusCurtius, not a medieval witness. Exact printed edition/year and Latin variants were not collated in this bounded pass. Anaporica spelling, eighth-division references and the hydraulic explanations remain this translation branch. Physical engineering adequacy is not certified. The prior analemma construction is an explicit prerequisite outside this bounded clock description.
complete_selected_source.unaltered_source_defect: The owned complete_text has an HTML/annotation fragment in §12 after Aries, including onMouseOut. Its source bytes are retained; this separate §9 boundary does not clean or certify the full excerpt. The source writes Anaporica in §8; the old anaphoric-clock card title is not new technical evidence.

full_content_obligations: The sand counterweight descends and turns the axis.
Rotation brings greater or smaller parts of the zodiac circle into motion, adjusting hours to seasons.
Each month sign has as many holes as days in that month.
The sun-shaped index shows hour spaces.
Passing from one hole to another completes the period of a month.

concrete_typed_sketch.entities: One float F, one sand counterweight C, axle X, wheel D and sun index I; month m and its ordered holes H(m). Identities remain fixed across operations.
concrete_typed_sketch.input: A water-rise episode acting on F in the declared apparatus. No dimensions, water quantity, pressure or velocity is assigned.
concrete_typed_sketch.coupled_outputs: UP(F) entails DOWN(C), TURN(X), then TURN(D) in the reported mechanism. The index changes position among holes of the same named month.
concrete_typed_sketch.month_binding: |H(m)| equals the supplied number of days of m, but no unstated numerical month lengths, starting-hole convention, day-transition off-by-one rule or next-month reset is invented. These details remain explicit debts for any executable calendar interpretation.

new_content_relative_to_completed_amulet: One part moving upward and another downward jointly causes axle/wheel motion and a changing display. This is a different process and outcome from assembly or commentary about a static amulet. The coupling is already owned by RAW394; this is a more narrowly bounded source sketch rather than claimed new mechanism discovery.
specific_competing_bindings: A reading that lets float and counterweight rise together predicts a different sign relationship under the same water-rise input.
A reading that treats the later wheel/index as an unrelated apparatus loses the first-to-later part identity and fails to connect the same driving motion to the changing display.
A uniform fixed-hour display can preserve the part names yet discard the passage’s stated greater/smaller seasonal behavior; this is an output difference, not a missing-name score.
strongest_countercases: The source translation’s engineering adequacy is not independently certified.
No continuous flow equation, 365-point regulator, astronomical ephemeris or exact hour duration follows from §9.
The index/day language leaves transition-count and calendar-boundary details unbound; implementing arbitrary month lengths would add source facts.
No Voynich picture or circle has been identified as this clock.
A source-only check would repeat RAW394 obligations without testing manuscript meaning.

missing_bindings.gap: No exact whole target paragraph or full target dictionary/grammar. The source sketch also lacks executable month-boundary conventions, so it is not a certified calendar simulation.
